name: nonApi_updateKennelCreditByUser
description: Recalculates the running payment credit balance for a single user (optionally scoped to one kennel) and writes the result back to three places: HC.Payment.CreditAvailable (per-payment running balance, SUM(NetPayment) over the kennel's payments ordered by the event's EventStartLocal — or PaidDate for a payment with no event — then payment id as tie-break), HC.HasherKennelMap.KennelCredit (the current balance everything reads), and HC.KennelCredit (legacy table, kept in sync until retired; a first-ever payment with no event cannot seed it because balanceAsOfEventId is NOT NULL). The payment → event join is a LEFT join on purpose: an INNER join silently dropped event-less payments (credit purchases, promotional grants) from the balance entirely. Only rows whose balance changes are written; each write stamps updatedAt (SYSDATETIMEOFFSET()) so the rows re-sync. Called (EXEC) inside and after transactions by portal and app payment SPs; internal, no auth. Returns nothing.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Hasher whose credit balances to recalculate.

parameters.name: kennelId
parameters.description: Scope to a single kennel. NULL = recalculate credit across all kennels for this user. Default NULL.

sideEffects: Updates HC.Payment.CreditAvailable and updatedAt for the user's uncancelled payments (optionally scoped to @kennelId) whose running balance changed.
Updates HC.HasherKennelMap.KennelCredit and updatedAt (row re-syncs) where the latest balance per kennel changed.

Updates HC.KennelCredit.currentBalance, balanceAsOfEventId (kept when the newest payment has no event), updatedAt where changed; inserts an HC.KennelCredit row where none exists, the balance is non-zero and the newest payment has an event.
Creates and drops #bal. Uses the IX_CreditBalance index hint on HC.Payment.

codeSmells.issue: HC.KennelCredit is a legacy table — kept in sync but marked for retirement
codeSmells.detail: The SP comment explicitly flags HC.KennelCredit as a legacy table to be removed when retired. Until then, every credit recalculation must maintain three separate tables. The dual-update pattern adds complexity and two additional write paths that must stay in sync.

The SP has no TRY/CATCH. An error in any of the three UPDATE/INSERT steps propagates as a raw exception to the caller. Since this SP is typically called inside a caller's transaction, a raw exception will roll back that transaction correctly — but partial updates within this SP body are possible if XACT_ABORT does not cover all cases.

@userId has no SQL default. Called only by EXEC from the payment SPs, which always pass it. A call that omits one fails before the body runs — no HC.ErrorLog row, no graceful check (CLAUDE.md 'SP parameter with NO default').
